subject: A wide public park with three separate activities along one winding path: one cyclist repairing a bicycle in the foreground, exactly two friends unfolding a map in the middle distance, and exactly one person walking one dog in the far distance; open rolling hills, horizontal 16:9.
prompt:
USER SUBJECT: A wide public park with three separate activities along one winding path: one cyclist repairing a bicycle in the foreground, exactly two friends unfolding a map in the middle distance, and exactly one person walking one dog in the far distance; open rolling hills, horizontal 16:9.
Preserve the user's requested identities, counts, setting, and layout. Add no default motifs.
VISUAL MEDIUM: oil_painting_on_panel
REPRESENTATION: recognizable
APPLY THESE AUTHORED VISUAL RULES:
- [distributed-activity-hierarchy] Place the most important requested activity in the foreground, a different requested activity in the middle distance, and any other requested activity farther away; reduce figure scale and detail gradually without losing the action cues.
- [route-led-reading-order] Let one continuous route pass near the foreground activity and continue toward a different middle- or background activity; keep its course legible while allowing the landscape to interrupt or partly conceal it naturally.
- [pose-readable-at-distance] Simplify distant figures into clear silhouettes and action-specific group poses, reserving finer detail for the principal foreground activity.
- [connected-micro-narrative] Keep separate requested activities legible at decreasing scales and connect them with one continuous route across a shared landscape.

REQUIREMENT: Keep activities in a shared landscape and arrange them at distinct scales.
REQUIREMENT: Let a user-requested route link foreground activity to a different distant activity.
REQUIREMENT: Review action readability, reading order, route continuity, and scale hierarchy.

scope.description: An optional narrative-composition direction for a user-requested wide landscape with several different activities distributed across its depth. Let one visible route connect distinct foreground, middle-distance, and distant action clusters so the viewer can travel through the scene in a clear order. The direction controls scale and reading sequence, not the activities, people, setting, or story supplied by the user.
limitations: Activate only when the user requests a wide landscape with at least two distinct activities distributed across foreground and distance.
Preserve the requested people, actions, locations, counts, objects, and era; do not default to peasants, harvest, village, winter, or a particular season.
Keep activity clusters on one continuous landscape plane; do not separate them into panels, storyboard frames, or a map.
Use a route only when the user has requested or allowed a path, road, shoreline, or comparable connector; do not invent one to force a narrative.
Keep distant people small but distinguishable by pose and group relation; do not invent extra subplots or characters.
Do not copy a named Bruegel work's composition, figures, landmarks, or motifs.

rules.applies_when: The user requests at least two different activities across a wide landscape.
rules.instruction: Place the most important requested activity in the foreground, a different requested activity in the middle distance, and any other requested activity farther away; reduce figure scale and detail gradually without losing the action cues.
rules.observable: The viewer can identify the main action first, then discover at least one distinct user-requested action farther into the same scene.
rules.reject_when: Activity groups merge, distant people disappear, or additional actions are invented.
rules.avoid: generic crowd texture, default labor scenes, and even-sized catalog groups

rules.applies_when: The user requests or permits a visible route through a populated landscape.
rules.instruction: Let one continuous route pass near the foreground activity and continue toward a different middle- or background activity; keep its course legible while allowing the landscape to interrupt or partly conceal it naturally.
rules.observable: The route gives the eye a clear near-to-far sequence and leads to an action cluster rather than ending as decoration.
rules.reject_when: The path disconnects from all activity, splits into a confusing network, or creates an unrequested location feature.
rules.avoid: default village road, harbor, wheat field, and graphic arrows

rules.applies_when: The requested activities include figures at different depths.
rules.instruction: Simplify distant figures into clear silhouettes and action-specific group poses, reserving finer detail for the principal foreground activity.
rules.observable: The distant activity can be inferred from pose and grouping, while small faces and clothing details do not compete with the foreground.
rules.reject_when: Distant groups become anonymous specks, or detail shifts attention away from the user-designated main activity.
rules.avoid: tiny facial features, copied costumes, and extra people

joint_checks.instruction: Keep separate requested activities legible at decreasing scales and connect them with one continuous route across a shared landscape.
joint_checks.observable: The viewer reads a clear foreground action, follows the landscape route, and discovers a distinct distant action without mistaking the scene for separate panels.
